title: U.S. House · Texas's 21st District
area: Central Texas, including parts of Austin, San Antonio and the Hill Country.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Chip Roy did not appear on the ballot in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for the redrawn 21st District. Mark Teixeira won the Republican nomination outright with 60.9% of the vote in a twelve-candidate field. Kristin Hook, who ran against Roy in 2024, won the Democratic nomination outright.

candidates.name: Kristin Hook
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.1% of the vote over Regina Vanburg and Gary Taylor.

summary.text: Kristin Hook is the Democratic nominee for this open Central Texas seat. A scientist with a Ph.D. in animal behavior from Cornell University, she taught middle school science through Teach for America before working as a researcher and then as a congressional oversight investigator in Sen. Elizabeth Warren's office, at the National Institutes of Health and at the Government Accountability Office. She ran against Rep. Chip Roy for this seat in 2024 and is running again in the redrawn district.

background.text: Born in Corpus Christi, Texas, and raised in a working-class family in South Texas, according to Ballotpedia and the Herald-Zeitung.

Earned two bachelor's degrees (biology and a humanities honors program) from the University of Texas at Austin in 2007, with help from scholarships and Pell grants, and a Ph.D. in animal behavior from Cornell University in 2016.
Joined Teach for America and spent three years teaching middle school science in New York City, according to her campaign website.

Worked as a postdoctoral researcher in reproductive biology at the University of Maryland; according to her campaign website, she organized grassroots efforts for women scientists in the Washington, D.C., area.

Moved into federal science and technology policy work in 2020: an oversight investigator in Sen. Elizabeth Warren's office through an American Association for the Advancement of Science fellowship, then the National Institutes of Health, then the Government Accountability Office as a biologist, which allowed her to return to Texas.
Ran as the Democratic nominee against Rep. Chip Roy in Texas's 21st District in 2024; Roy won with 61% of the vote.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.1% of the vote, defeating Regina Vanburg and Gary Taylor, for the seat opened when Roy ran for Texas attorney general.

priorities.text: Running to fight for affordability, expand opportunity, and demand accountability for working Texans.
priorities.quote: I'm running to fight for affordability, expand opportunity, and demand accountability for working Texans.

priorities.text: Says her GAO experience protecting tax dollars from waste, fraud and abuse and advising Congress on emerging technologies like AI prepares her for oversight work.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she will defend and strengthen the Affordable Care Act, CHIP and Medicare and protect Medicaid funding and access.
positions.quote: Protecting Medicaid funding and access and fighting restrictive eligibility requirements

positions.summary: Her campaign website says her first priority will be legislation restoring the right to an abortion nationwide.
positions.quote: my first priority will be to introduce, co-sponsor, and support legislation that restores the right to an abortion nationwide.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she will support legislation reforming the tax code so billionaires and corporations pay their fair share.
positions.quote: Reforms our tax code so billionaires and corporations pay their fair share

positions.summary: Her campaign website lists raising the federal minimum wage among the legislation she will support.
positions.quote: Raises the federal minimum wage and addresses income inequality

positions.summary: Her campaign website lists making housing more affordable by capping rent increases among the legislation she will support.
positions.quote: Makes housing more affordable, such as by capping rent increases

positions.summary: Her campaign website opposes the state school voucher program and says public dollars belong in public schools.
positions.quote: I believe public dollars belong in public schools and will always put Texan families first.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she will fight for advancing clean energy technologies, investments and incentives and for slashing pollution.
positions.quote: Advancing clean energy technologies, investments, and incentives

candidates.name: Mark Teixeira
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 60.9% of the vote over eleven other candidates.

summary.text: Mark Teixeira is the Republican nominee for this open Central Texas seat. A former Major League Baseball first baseman who won a World Series with the New York Yankees in 2009, he moved back to Texas in 2021. He won the 12-candidate Republican primary on March 3, 2026, and campaigns on border security, cutting federal spending, and energy production.

background.text: Grew up in Severna Park, Maryland, and attended Mount Saint Joseph High School, according to The Baltimore Banner. His campaign website says his father was a Navy veteran and his mother a schoolteacher.
Attended the Georgia Institute of Technology on a scholarship and received a bachelor's degree in business administration; he met his wife, Leigh, there, according to his campaign website.
Drafted fifth overall by the Texas Rangers in the 2001 MLB draft after his junior season.
Played 14 Major League seasons for the Texas Rangers, Atlanta Braves, Los Angeles Angels and New York Yankees, with three All-Star selections, five Gold Gloves and three Silver Sluggers.
Won the World Series with the Yankees in 2009.

According to his campaign website, received the 2018 Heisman Humanitarian Award, was a two-time finalist for the Roberto Clemente Award, and has served on boards supporting youth sports and college scholarships; FOX 7 Austin lists him as a member of the board of directors of DREAM.
Moved his family back to Texas in 2021 after retiring from baseball, per The Baltimore Banner.

Announced his run for the seat after Rep. Chip Roy said he would run for Texas attorney general instead of seeking re-election; won the 12-candidate Republican primary on March 3, 2026, with 60.9% of the vote.
According to his campaign website, he and Leigh have three children and are active in their local church.

priorities.text: Lists border security and immigration enforcement, cutting federal spending, and energy independence among his campaign priorities.
priorities.quote: Fully secure the southern border, deport illegal aliens, and crush the cartels to keep Texans safe.

priorities.text: Says he wants to expand DOGE's federal spending cuts and enact congressional term limits.
priorities.quote: Expand DOGE to cut insane wasteful spending, rein in the Deep State, and grow the economy by putting taxpayers first.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for fully securing the southern border and deporting people in the country illegally.
positions.quote: Fully secure the southern border, deport illegal aliens, and crush the cartels to keep Texans safe.

statements.quote: Unleash Texas oil, gas, and nuclear to restore U.S. energy dominance and drive down costs for families.
